reports.title: Marathon Petroleum Corp. Reports Third-Quarter 2026 Results

lines: MPLX will receive $750 million of the proceeds, representing a 9x multiple on forecast 2027 adjusted EBITDA of the associated logistics assets.
MPC’s 2026 capital spending outlook (excluding MPLX) is $1.5 billion.

desk.headline: Adjusted EPS jumps to $26.93 on refining margins, beat; Q4 operating outlook given, dividend up 10% and $5bn more buybacks
results: Net income attributable to MPC rose to $7.4bn ($26.59 a share) from $1.4bn; adjusted EPS was $26.93 versus $3.01 a year ago.
Refining drove the jump: segment adjusted EBITDA reached $9.9bn ($34.15 a barrel) as crack spreads rose in all regions and refineries ran at 100% of capacity.
Midstream adjusted EBITDA rose to $1.9bn and renewable diesel swung to a $254m profit from a loss.
Total revenues and other income rose 58% to $56.5bn; cash and short-term investments were $13.6bn at quarter end, with no revolver borrowings.
$3.3bn went back to shareholders; the board added a $5bn buyback authorisation and raised the quarterly dividend 10%. The St. Paul Park and Mandan refineries are being sold for $4.2bn.

guidance.summary: MPC gives no earnings forecast; it set Q4 operating targets (lower throughput as maintenance rises) and a 2026 capital budget of $1.5bn excluding MPLX.

points: CEO Maryann Mannen expects strong refining margins to last at least to mid-2027, pointing to tight global refining capacity and low US fuel stocks.
Margin capture was about 93%; weaker prices for secondary products and jet fuel are expected to keep weighing in Q4.
The Mid-Con refinery sale is to CVR Energy; proceeds are to be reinvested mainly in Gulf Coast refineries.
MPLX distributions to MPC of about $3.1bn a year are expected to more than cover MPC's dividend and its own capital spending.
Q4 refinery utilisation is planned at about 95%, per the call coverage.
call.source: Call coverage: Zacks Equity Research via Yahoo Finance, 4 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Whether refining margins hold near current highs into 2027.
Closing of the $4.2bn Mid-Con refinery sale at year-end and where the proceeds go.
Pace of buybacks under the enlarged $8.1bn authorisation.
